thread_text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High tail latency detected for hosted-api-prod (generation endpoints). p95 and p99 breach. Auto-paging to eng-runtime on-call. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/latency?range=5m

samir: I'm on call. Acknowledging. Starting triage — grabbing logs and perf counters.

maya: seeing customer reports of streaming stalls and partial responses, some connection resets. Any correlation with deployments?

samir: no deploys in the last 30m (deploy-bot shows no successful deploys). Suspect runtime/inference layer. Pulling metrics now.

ops-bot: METRICS SNAPSHOT:
```
p50: 120ms
p95: 2.4s (baseline ~180ms)
p99: 6.2s (baseline ~450ms)
error_rate: 0.62% (↑)
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.34 (↓ from 0.82)
kv_cache_eviction_rate: 0.78 evictions/s (↑)
streaming_stalls: 34 events in last 10m
active_streams: 12.4k
```

eli: kv_cache_hit_ratio collapse + high eviction rate strongly points to cache pressure / fragmentation. Could be prefill workers inserting lots of long prefixes, crowding out decode cache entries. Seen similar when prefill vs decode imbalance occurs.

samir: running quick check on kv shards to confirm fragmentation and per-shard eviction hotspots.

samir: (exec) 
```
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/kv-shard-7 --tail=200 | egrep "eviction|frag_ratio|prefill"
[2026-03-14T18:02:11Z] WARN kv_cache: eviction triggered; frag_ratio=0.82; prefill_inserts=34567; decode_reads=9876
[2026-03-14T18:02:23Z] WARN kv_cache: eviction triggered; frag_ratio=0.85; slot_fill=0.92
[2026-03-14T18:03:05Z] INFO kv_cache: rebalancer queued 3 shards for compaction
```

maya: frag_ratio ~0.82 - pretty bad. That explains tail latency: many decode misses -> fall back to slower path, streaming stalls when KV lookups block on eviction/compaction.

eli: mitigation options (live):
- throttle prefill workers to reduce new large-key inserts
- increase cache.size config (if headroom exists on nodes)
- trigger targeted shard compaction/rebalance (cheap but can be I/O heavy)
- route heavy prefix tenants to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint

samir: trying a quick, reversible change: reduce prefill concurrency from 32 -> 8 for 5m and bump kv_cache.max_entries by 20% on affected nodes. Applying now.

samir: (run) `infractl rollout-set inference/kv_cache.prefill_concurrency=8 --env prod --target=kv-shard-* --expedite`

ops-bot: rollout started: 6/6 kv shards targeted.

samir: also bumping max_entries on shard-5,6,7: `infractl patch kv-shard-5 --set cache.max_entries=1.2x` (will monitor memory).

ops-bot: Memory pressure check: node-az3 memory used before change 78%, after patch 80% — within safe margin.

(5m later)
ops-bot: CHECKPOINT METRICS:
```
p50: 110ms
p95: 380ms
p99: 1.1s
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.68
kv_cache_eviction_rate: 0.12
streaming_stalls: 4 events last 5m
```

maya: nice, big improvement. Pre-fill throttle + extra capacity helped. p99 still above baseline but much better.

eli: for longer-term we should: switch to segmented-LRU (to avoid long-key eviction bias), add per-tenant cache quotas, and adjust prefill sizing heuristics (cap prefill key length). I'll file a follow-up.

samir: creating follow-up ticket: INF-3871 "KV cache fragmentation -> segLRU + per-tenant quotas" and assigning to eng-runtime/eli + eng-infra.

samir: status update to customers and execs? Do we need an incident page?

maya: yes, update status page with partial degradation and mitigation in progress. No data loss, just latency/streaming stalls for a subset of requests.

statusbot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-14-kv-cache-latency (message id: 7821).

samir: handing off to next on-call for follow-up changes and monitoring: @kendall you're up for the next shift — ping me if you want me to stay on for the postmortem.

kendall: taking handoff. Can you paste the runbooks/commands you used and the ticket link? I'll also keep an eye on p99 for next 2h.

samir: paste runbook snippets below and linking INF-3871.
```
# quick mitigations used in prod
infractl rollout-set inference/kv_cache.prefill_concurrency=8 --env prod --target=kv-shard-*
infractl patch kv-shard-5 --set cache.max_entries=1.2x
kubectl exec -n inference kv-shard-7 -- ./kv-tool compaction --target 3
# metrics to watch
metric: inference.latency.p95, inference.latency.p99, kv_cache.eviction_rate, kv_cache.frag_ratio, streaming.stalls
```

eli: also recommend adding a synthetic test that exercises prefill-heavy patterns to catch regressions in CI.

samir: agreed. Postmortem + action items:
- short-term: tune prefill defaults, add an automatic temp throttle when eviction rate > 0.5
- mid-term: implement segmented-LRU and per-tenant quotas (INF-3871)
- long-term: smarter prefill heuristics and cache-aware routing for heavy tenants

maya: customer comms note: flagged top affected tenants and sent outbound message via CSMs; no further escalations so far.

statusbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigation deployed). Final metrics: p95=160ms, p99=480ms, kv_cache_hit=0.83. Closing alert and opening postmortem draft (INF-3871). :white_check_mark:

samir: thanks team. Leaving notes in ops-runbook and passing to kendall for follow-up.

kendall: ack, will own postmortem.
